comment: "sedentibus super terram" = those sitting upon the earth (Douay "sit"); "dwell" reflects the KJV/TR reading. Only change made.
"misit in lacum" has no expressed object; "it" is the minimal supplement, "the grapes" was an added noun. Only change made.
"accepi a Patre meo" has no object; "authority" was supplied (from v.26 potestatem). Literal rendering matches Douay. Only change made.
"incipiam te evomere" = I will begin to vomit (Douay); "I am about to" renders Greek mellō. Only change made.
Latin distinguishes "sedilia" (seats) from following "thronos"; new English mirrors that. Only change made.
"septem lampades ardentes" lacks "of fire" (Greek pyros); "burned" covers ardentes. Only change made.
"tempus non erit amplius" = time shall be no longer (Douay); "no further delay" is the Greek-based interpretation. Only change made.

Dative plural "multis" after the series can be read over the whole list; Douay renders "to many nations, and peoples, and tongues, and kings." Old English was an acceptable reading; new is also accurate.
"dabo duobus testibus meis" has no object; "grant authority" supplied from Greek. New matches Douay "I will give unto my two witnesses". Only change made.
"rufus" = red (Douay "red"); "fiery" reflects Greek pyrros. Only change made.
"reget" = will rule (Douay); "shepherd" renders Greek poimanei. Only change made.
"candido" = white (Douay "glittering and white"); "clean" reflects Greek katharon/KJV. Only change made.
